sources.note: No prose on tone; every form carries Chao tone values from Chen's transcription. In the 274 Yaogao rows read (first 830 KB of) the tone strings are 13 (130x), 31 (72), 53 (59), 44 (44), 35 (38), 22 (37), 241 (33), 24 (14), 33 (8) - eight or nine distinct values (24 vs 241 possibly one category), i.e. an eight-tone-type system for the Rongshui southern point; the printed source (Chen 2013: 299) holds the actual tone table.

sources.note: Glottolog 63963 language note lists Purnell's Miao points incl. 'Jung-chiang = Rongjiang Miao = Miao-Southern Qiandong [hms]' (Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist, 38 pp.). The Jung-chiang point in this literature is Chang Kun's Kao-t'ung-chai 高同寨 (Rongjiang) field data, whose eight-tone system Chang 1973 tabulates (see missed work 6); Purnell's PMY tone-category reconstruction therefore includes a Southern Qiandong reflex set, but no page of Purnell was seen here.
